question: Barbara Allen was a favourite of Appalachian singers. Where is the ballad first recorded?
options: In a Scottish songbook of the 1790s
answer: In a London diary of 1666. On 2 January that year Samuel Pepys wrote of hearing the actress Mrs Knipp sing her little Scotch song of Barbary Allen. Allan Ramsay printed a text in Edinburgh in 1740. It went on to become one of the most widely collected ballads in North America.
move: Where a thing was found last says little about where it began.
trap: The Appalachian field notes, because that is where the song lived.
reference: Latham and Matthews (eds), The Diary of Samuel Pepys, vol. 7, G. Bell and Sons, 1972
